body:
GOAL
A zmx with opinions, shipped from this repo: a shell wrapper installed by overlay as `zmx`, an Emacs plugin on top of it, one vocabulary page, and nothing else.

DEFINITION OF DONE
- `nix build .#zmx` produces a wrapper; overlays.default installs it as `zmx`; the raw binary stays addressable at ${pkgs.zmx}/bin/zmx.
- Creating `project.id` writes `project` and `id` labels on the same call, and runs inside a transient systemd scope wherever a user systemd is usable.
- `zmx run` brackets the dispatch with `state=working` then `state=done|failed`, exits with the task's own code, and passes output through untouched.
- Every other verb and alias passes through byte-for-byte, including when invoked from inside a session.
- ZMX_RAW=1 disables every rewrite; ZMX_LAUNCHER="" disables the launcher; neither may break the primary verb when the launcher is unusable.
- No Rust crate remains in the repo, and the flake no longer pulls crane or rust-overlay.
- VOCABULARY.md exists and says only what the decision entities say.
- emacs/dl-zmx.el carries no naming, no label derivation and no `zmx list` parsing of its own.

NON-GOALS
A reader (`zmux ls`), a picker, a TUI, a daemon, a manifest, an MCP server, vendored forks of zp or pi-zmx, ZMX_SESSION_PREFIX support, and any automation of `blocked`.

ORDER
vocabulary -> tests -> wrapper -> drop the crate -> elisp -> flake wiring.

WHY THIS SHAPE
Every decision behind it is in the store: d-wrapper, d-install, d-birth, d-naming, d-name-form, d-vocab, d-state-writer, and the constraints c-cgroup, c-wrapper-limits, c-devjail, c-host-only, c-json-intolerant. Read brief-v0 first.
title: v0: the wrapped-zmx kit
